neighbours.label: 'still' marking that a state continues (still feel, still have)
fire: I'm thirty now, but in some ways I still feel like a teenager.
Years after the move, she still keeps her old house key.
The bakery on the corner is still open after midnight.
Even after the repair, the engine still makes that noise.
My grandfather still walks to the market every morning.
After all these years the song still gives me chills.
The bridge was damaged, but traffic is still moving slowly.
Despite the warning, many residents still refuse to leave.
quiet: I'm thirty now, and in most ways I finally feel like an adult.
Years after the move, she finally lost her old house key.
The bakery on the corner is now closed after midnight.
After the repair, the engine no longer makes that noise.
My grandfather used to walk to the market every morning.
The first time I heard the song it gave me chills.
The bridge was damaged, so traffic was moved to a detour.
After the warning, most residents agreed to leave.

notes: card: top 32 led by ' still' x4, mixed with clause punctuation; output (+ pole) promotes still/remain/retain, so this pole sits on the continuation side
